key_insight: Density-matrix propagation provides a practical maximum-likelihood benchmark for small quantum codes, revealing that common decoders can be near-optimal for repetition codes but substantially suboptimal for cellular automaton codes under circuit-level noise.
engineering_relevance: This gives quantum error-correction engineers a way to quantify decoder gap versus optimal performance, helping guide decoder choice, noise-model validation, and code-specific design tradeoffs.
method: Propagate the full density matrix through syndrome-extraction rounds to evaluate optimal decoding for each syndrome history.
Use pruning with rigorous bounds to reduce the number of histories that must be tracked.
Benchmark MWPM, BP+OSD, Tesseract, and Planar decoders against the maximum-likelihood reference.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports evaluations on small repetition-code and cellular-automaton-code instances under circuit-level noise, showing standard decoders stay close to optimal for repetition code but can deviate strongly for the cellular automaton code, especially BP+OSD.
watch_item: The framework is currently limited to small codes and relies on pruning approximations with bounds, so scaling to larger architectures and deeper circuits remains a key implementation challenge.
paper_title: Optimal Decoding of Small Codes by Density Matrix Propagation
